datapoints.unit: app restaurant-delivery workers working 'in any given week'
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, 'A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC' (Nov 2022), Workforce Size
datapoints.verbatim: The Department estimates that as of the second quarter of 2022, 61,000 delivery workers were working for restaurant apps in NYC in any given week. ... in the fourth quarter of 2021 there were 219,787 worker accounts associated with at least one delivery in NYC. After adjusting for multi-apping, the Department estimates that these accounts were held by 122,104 individuals ... 39% of the unique worker phone numbers in the Department's data were associated with deliveries in two or fewer weeks.
datapoints.notes: Key ratio for the caller: weekly-active (61,000) / quarterly-unique individuals (122,104) = 0.50; accounts per individual = 1.80 (multi-apping). Later official updates: Mayor's Office 2024-07-11: 'more than 60,000 app-based delivery workers in our city' (high; https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/news/539-24/new-report-shows-mayor-adams-commissioner-mayuga-deliver-delivery-workers-significantly). NYSERDA Report 25-38 (Dec 2025): 'Over 65,000 delivery workers rely on micromobility to distribute food, groceries, and packages across New York City's (NYC) five boroughs' (medium-high; https://www.nyserda.ny.gov/-/media/Project/Nyserda/Files/Publications/Research/Transportation/25-38-NYC-Delivery-Worker-Data-Collection-and-Research-Report.pdf). A search summary also cited 'an estimated 80,000 workers who earned at least $1,500 making deliveries in 2024' -- primary source NOT verified (low).

datapoints.unit: app restaurant deliveries per year (Jul 2021-Jun 2022), four largest apps
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP Nov 2022 study
datapoints.verbatim: The four largest (Uber Eats, Grubhub, DoorDash, and Relay) are responsible for nearly all app deliveries in NYC (99%), performing 124 million deliveries in NYC between July 2021 and June 2022.
datapoints.notes: = ~2.38M deliveries/week; ~39 deliveries per weekly-active worker per week (124M/52/61,000). Update: Mayor's Office 2024-07-11 press: 'The number of deliveries increased by 8 percent -- from more than 2.56 million in Q1 2023 to more than 2.77 million in Q1 2024' (unit reads as weekly average; consistent with ~2.4M/week in 2021-22). Average delivery distance 1.77 miles (DCWP 2022).

datapoints.value: Workers: car 43.9%, non-car 56.1% (e-bike 46.1%, walking 8.7%, motorcycle 1.3%). Hours: car 30.6%, non-car 69.4% (e-bike 54.1%). Deliveries: car 22.4%, non-car 77.7% (e-bike 65.8%, walking 10.2%, motorcycle 1.7%).
datapoints.unit: % of app delivery workers / hours / deliveries by mode
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP Nov 2022 study, Table 3 'App Delivery Workers, Hours, and Deliveries, by Mode of Transportation, NYC, Fourth Quarter 2021' (record-level app data)
datapoints.verbatim: Based on the apps' data, non-car modes of transportation account for 56% of workers but 69% of hours worked and 78% of deliveries. ... Table 3: Non-Car 56.1 | 69.4 | 77.7 | 22.2 hrs/wk | 1.869 deliveries/hr; E-bike 46.1 | 54.1 | 65.8 | 21.3 | 2.030; Walking 8.7 | 13.5 | 10.2 | 25.7 | 1.266; Motorcycle 1.3 | 1.8 | 1.7 | 25.2 | 1.530; Car 43.9 | 30.6 | 22.4 | 17.5 | 1.128
datapoints.notes: VERIFIES the '44% car' claim: 43.9% of WORKERS used a car as primary mode, but cars did only 22.4% of DELIVERIES. DCWP cautions many moped users self-report as 'e-bike', so 46.1% e-bike = e-bike + moped. Productivity: e-bike 2.03 deliveries/hr vs car 1.13; non-car 22.2 hrs/wk vs car 17.5. DCWP also notes 'a steady movement away from cars' Jan 2021-2022. NYSERDA Dec 2025 intercept survey (n>300, micromobility users only): personal e-bikes 47.9%, rental e-bikes 24.4%, gas mopeds 13.4%, e-mopeds 7.2%, pedal bikes remainder; screenline observations 74.4% personal e-bikes; Manhattan personal e-bikes 51.8%; Brooklyn personal e-bike 34.7% vs gas moped 29.2%; 65% of gas-moped users previously used e-modes.

datapoints.unit: % of DoorDash deliveries on two wheels
datapoints.source: DoorDash 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report p.7

datapoints.unit: unique app-based delivery workers covered over first 18 months (Jan 15 2024 - Jun 29 2025), five largest network companies
datapoints.geography: Seattle (workers performing offers in Seattle; 74.7% live outside city limits)
datapoints.source: Seattle Office of Labor Standards, 'Seattle's App-Based Worker Minimum Payment Ordinance (SMC 8.37), the First Report' (April 2026)
datapoints.verbatim: During the first eighteen months of implementation, the ordinance covered 92,801 workers working for the five largest network companies. ... Across all complete quarters shown, there was an average of 34,646 unique engaged workers per quarter. ... there were on average 15,489 engaged worker accounts per week. From Half 1 2024 to Half 1 2025 ... average weekly engaged workers accounts from 14,345 to 16,200 worker accounts (+1,855 or 12.9%). ... More than 85% of the workers only worked on one app. ... In Quarter 2 2025, 25.3% of engaged worker accounts were located within Seattle city limits, whereas 74.7% of worker accounts lived outside.
datapoints.notes: Key ratios: weekly engaged accounts (~15.5-16.2k; ~13.5-14k unique workers after >85% single-app) / quarterly unique (34,646) = ~0.45; quarterly unique / 18-month unique = 0.37. Five companies = DoorDash, Uber Eats, Instacart, Grubhub, Amazon Flex (covers grocery + package, not only restaurant). Seattle city pop ~781k -> weekly engaged accounts = ~2.0% of pop; quarterly unique = ~4.4% of pop.

datapoints.unit: completed offers per week (avg over Jan 2024-Jun 2025), five largest network companies
datapoints.source: Seattle OLS SMC 8.37 Data Report (April 2026), Market Volume
datapoints.verbatim: there was an average of 196,871 offers per week completed by the five largest companies. From Half 1 2024 to Half 1 2025 ... average weekly offers from 197,148 offers to 203,469 offers (+6,321 offers per week or +3.2%).
datapoints.notes: ~12.7 offers per engaged worker account per week; ~0.25 offers per resident per week. Engaged hours: 'an average of 7.3 engaged hours per worker account per week' (7.4 -> 7.5); Key Takeaways: 'On average, app-based workers worked 12 hours per week per app' (likely incl. available time). Base pay $30.12/engaged hr after mileage; $36.36 incl. tips/bonuses.

datapoints.unit: USD gross hourly delivery earnings (national, Gridwise users), Q4 2025
datapoints.source: Gridwise Analytics 2026 Annual Gig Mobility Report (via Food On Demand / PRNewswire summaries)
datapoints.verbatim: Hourly delivery earnings rose 3.2 percent between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, reaching $14.66 late last year ... Uber Eats drivers saw a 5% drop in hourly pay to $14.96, DoorDash drivers' hourly earnings fell by 3% to $12.23 ... Tips per trip slipped to $4.16 in Q4 2025
datapoints.notes: Relayed from search summaries; Gridwise report page not fetched. Gridwise city-level LA delivery data (orders/hour, earnings) not located -- see gaps. Contrast with DoorDash's Prop 22 on-delivery figure for LA ($35/hr in 2023, active-time only, incl. tips).

gaps: Uber Eats: no LA courier-mode statement or courier count found; Uber does not split Delivery trips from total Trips (13,567M FY2025).

DoorDash US-vs-international order split for FY2025 not disclosed in the Q4 press release; the 10-K (revenue by geography) was not fetched. Proxy: 'over 3 million deliveries/day' US in 2024 vs 2.58B global orders 2024.

Bloomberg Second Measure has not published a post-April-2024 update of the meal-delivery share series; 2025-2026 shares available only from low-reliability aggregators (DoorDash ~56-61%, Uber Eats ~23-26%, Grubhub ~6-16%). Earnest/YipitData LA-metro share of US delivery spend not found.

No published count of Dashers/couriers for Los Angeles or California (DoorDash Public First microsite exposes national aggregates only; Prop 22 post says 'hundreds of thousands of California Dashers').
San Francisco: no verified count of active app couriers ('Underscore SF ~2,000' could not be located); only pilot cohort sizes (30 -> 60+ riders).
Gridwise/Solo LA-specific delivery metrics (orders/hour, hourly earnings) not located; only national Q4 2025 figures.

NYC: the '80,000 workers earning >= $1,500 in 2024' figure surfaced in a search summary but its primary source (DCWP grocery-worker rule or Comptroller) was not verified. NYC DOHMH total restaurant count not fetched (DCWP's ~23,000 used instead). Restaurants-on-apps only inferable from DCWP survey shares (61-67% per major app).
Seattle restaurant count only from a Google-listings scrape (1,598); King County permitted-establishment count not fetched. Seattle OLS report has no vehicle-mode breakdown.

Population: LA metro (12,974,487) relayed from USAFacts summary; LA County 2024 (9,757,179), US 2024 (340,110,988), Seattle (780,995), SF (827,526) are recalled Census Vintage 2024 values not fetched directly (LA County 2025 = 9,694,934 was fetched from FRED). LA city 3,878,704 and NYC 8,478,072 were fetched from the Census press release.
Axios articles (SF 2025-02-26, national map 2025-02-25, SD 2026-03-19) return 403 directly and via web.archive.org; their figures are corroborated by the DoorDash 2026 report table instead.

DoorDash 2025 (first-edition) Two-Wheeled Report city figures for 2024 not separately extracted (Axios summary: SF 72%, Seattle 66%, San Jose 64%, NYC 58%, DC 57% for 2024) -- note NYC moved 58% -> 55% and DC 57% -> 54% in the 2025-data edition, so LA's 2024 value is unknown but likely within a few points of 49%.

Sub-city (Downtown LA / Koreatown / Westlake / USC) two-wheel or courier data: none published by any platform; DoorDash report only notes two-wheel trips under 2 miles move >=10% faster than cars in dense cores.
